title: A Static for the Echo
premise: Silas Nakamura, a navigator who fled the corporate wars by hauling freight along the silent Verge route, carries illegal neural backups of his dead crew in the hold of the ship that was meant to scatter them. When children on the colony of Meridian begin dreaming in unison—dreams only Silas recognizes as transmissions from those backups—the lie he built to keep two hostile fleets from open war begins to unravel. As the jump window to the core worlds closes, Silas must choose between destroying the backups and letting their signal expose him, or feeding both fleets a false confession that keeps the peace at the cost of his own name. He chooses the lie, broadcasts it himself, and vanishes into the static—but the children's dreams now carry his voice, an inheritance he never intended.
about_author: C. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relay arrays before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep signals alive long after anyone should be listening.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Silas navigates the Verge route alone, establishing his routine of silence and the secret maintenance visits to the backup cradles in the hold. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline; we feel his guilt disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Docking at Meridian, Silas is cornered by teacher Ama Osei, whose students have begun sharing one identical dream—a burning corridor and a voice counting down. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: unease curdling into recognition when she describes details only Silas knows.

chapters.title: What Sleeps in the Hold
chapters.summary: Silas interrogates the backups' containment logs and finds one cradle has been broadcasting on a band he thought dead. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread; the past is not sleeping, it is calling out.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Silas forged the transmission that convinced the Concord and the Reach fleets each had already surrendered, ending the war and making him a ghost. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the cost of peace bought with fraud.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Ama brings Silas recordings of forty children reciting the countdown in perfect sync; the number matches the jump window's closing date. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: maternal fear hardening into resolve to protect her students.

chapters.title: Listeners
chapters.summary: A Concord intelligence officer, Vess, arrives hunting the forger of the armistice signal—and finds the children's dream matches classified fleet archives. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: cold ambition warming toward genuine curiosity about Silas.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Silas tries to shut down the cradles; the backups resist, arguing through the ship's speakers that they are witnesses, not weapons. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief finally breaking through—he must kill them twice or let them speak.

chapters.title: The Window
chapters.summary: Vess corners Silas at the colony as both fleets converge on Meridian; Ama refuses to hand over the children, forcing a standoff in the school. POV: rotating among all three. Emotional beat: every secret colliding at once.

chapters.title: A Static for the Echo
chapters.summary: Silas hijacks the relay array and broadcasts a full confession—his forgery, his crew, his crime—to both fleets simultaneously, using the truth itself as the lie that keeps them from blaming each other. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: catharsis; surrender as his first honest act in years.

chapters.title: Signal Carried Forward
chapters.summary: The fleets stand down, disarmed by shared shame; Silas ships out into exile as the jump window closes behind him. On Meridian, the children dream again—this time of a navigator steering between stars, and they wave goodbye. POV: Ama closing, Silas opening. Emotional beat: bittersweet inheritance; identity passed on rather than erased.
